titlePlain: Pagination: TOP vs. ROWNUM/FETCH FIRST vs.
subtitle: Lesson 12 · Querying Basics Compared

eyebrow: SQL Server: TOP limits, OFFSET/FETCH pages
caption: TOP only limits row count — it has no concept of skipping rows.

eyebrow: Oracle's classic trap: ROWNUM before ORDER BY
code:
-- WRONG: ROWNUM is assigned BEFORE ORDER BY runs
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Products
WHERE ROWNUM <= 10
ORDER BY ListPrice DESC;
caption: This filters 10 arbitrary rows first, then sorts them — not the top 10 by price.

eyebrow: The fix: sort in a subquery, then number
caption: Modern Oracle also supports the ANSI-standard FETCH FIRST syntax.

code:
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Products
ORDER BY ListPrice DESC
LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10;
caption: Both platforms share this syntax; PostgreSQL also accepts OFFSET/FETCH.
